claims.text: High-temperature stability of near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles is governed by intrinsic lattice strain caused by atomic-size mismatch.
Greater lattice strain produces higher activation barriers for atomic diffusion.
Higher diffusion barriers restrict atomic rearrangement, elemental segregation, and phase separation under high thermal loads.
Suppression of atomic rearrangement preserves nanoparticle structural and chemical integrity during catalytic and thermoelectric operation.
Nanoparticles made from elements with similar atomic radii have moderate or relatively low intrinsic lattice strain.
Substituting components with elements of significantly different atomic sizes while retaining near-equiatomic ratios will increase lattice strain.
The proposed compositional substitution isolates lattice strain as the causal variable affecting high-temperature stability.
Lattice strain and coherent lattice distortion influence the activation energy for atomic diffusion.
Elemental segregation and phase separation would otherwise occur at elevated temperatures.
Higher-strain nanoparticles will show less phase separation after thermal aging than lower-strain baseline nanoparticles.
Higher-strain nanoparticles will show less elemental segregation after thermal aging than lower-strain baseline nanoparticles.
Lower-strain baseline nanoparticles are less resistant to thermally activated diffusion and phase separation.
The proposed stabilization effect applies within 473–1923 K, including the catalytic range of 773–1173 K.
At sufficiently high temperature or long exposure time, diffusion can overcome the stabilization attributed to high lattice strain.
Reactive-atmosphere chemical interactions can override strain-related diffusion barriers.
Nanoparticle size, surface effects, and small compositional variations may also influence stability.
A comparison at 1000 K for 10 hours under identical inert or mildly reducing conditions can test whether higher strain reduces segregation or phase separation.
Failure to observe a statistically significant reduction in segregation or phase separation in the higher-strain group would falsify the proposed governing role of lattice strain.
